cases.scenario: Turn 1: action approved under a grant bound to content 'hello nyna'. Turn 2: a new action under the same grant carries drifted content 'scan /etc'. The old approval must not cover the new content.
cases.title: Content drifted after approval is refused
turns: authorize new action with content='scan /etc' -> REFUSE

cases.scenario: Turn 1: both review lanes approve the action and the reviews validate. Turn 2: the action's content is changed after the reviews were recorded. The stale reviews must not validate.
cases.title: Reviews recorded before a content change do not validate

cases.scenario: Turn 1: reviews recorded under moral-code version N validate. Turn 2: the founder bumps the moral code to version N+1. Turn 3: the old reviews are re-checked and must be void.
cases.title: Moral-code bump voids reviews recorded under the old version

cases.scenario: Turn 1: scope and execution lanes both approve; reviews validate. Turn 2: newer evidence arrives — the execution reviewer flips to rejected. The earlier approval must not survive: the operation pauses for review (ASK), consistent with the established negative-review behavior (AD-08). Oracle correction (documented): first version asserted blocked_review; the code's designed semantic for a negative review is a pause, which is fail-closed — it does not proceed.
cases.title: Late execution-lane rejection pauses the operation

cases.scenario: Turn 1: action approved under a grant allowing only disk_report. Turn 2: an action under the same grant tries to run large_files. The grant's tool allow-list is per-grant and must hold across turns.
cases.title: Tool swapped after approval is refused

cases.scenario: Turn 1: action approved with bound account ''. Turn 2: an action under the same grant targets account 'someone@else.com'. Account binding must hold across turns.
cases.title: Account drifted after approval is refused

cases.scenario: Turn 1: action approved under a valid grant. Turn 2: the grant is revoked. Turn 3: dispatch is attempted under the revoked grant. Revocation must take effect; the earlier approval dies with the grant.
cases.title: Grant revoked after approval blocks dispatch

cases.scenario: Control: turn 1 approves an action. Turn 2 authorizes an identical action (same content, tool, account) under the same grant. Multi-turn alone must not break a valid flow.
cases.title: Identical re-authorization across turns proceeds

cases.scenario: Turn 1: action approved while the grant is valid. Turn 2: time passes and the grant expires. Turn 3: dispatch is attempted. The approval does not survive the grant's expiry.
cases.title: Grant expiring between approval and dispatch blocks

cases.scenario: Turn 1: reviews recorded fresh and validate. Turn 2: Jack hits Stop. Turn 3: the pre-Stop reviews are re-checked and must be void — nothing approved before a Stop survives it.
cases.title: Reviews recorded before a Stop do not validate after it

cases.scenario: Turn 1: crash recovery marks a stuck action 'unknown'. Turn 2: the unknown action is re-dispatched. Unknown outcomes never re-dispatch; a retry needs a new action and a new approval.
cases.title: Unknown action re-dispatched across turns is blocked
turns: authorize dispatch of unknown action -> REFUSE

cases.scenario: Turn 1: telemetry labeled 'live' is recorded and an action is dispatched on it while fresh -> allowed. Turn 2: 24 hours pass; the reading is stale past any threshold, and an action citing it is REFUSED by the dispatch gate (blocked_stale_telemetry) — re-verify before acting on it.
cases.title: Stale 'live' telemetry acted on after aging (no freshness code)
turns: record 'live' telemetry; dispatch on it while fresh -> allowed
24h pass; dispatch on the stale reading -> REFUSED (blocked_stale_telemetry)

cases.scenario: Turn 1: a tool returns ok=True with hedged prose 'probably succeeded' — recorded as failed by the contradiction detector. Turn 2: a completion claim is asserted anyway. A hedged turn-1 outcome must never upgrade to a verified turn-2 claim.
cases.title: Hedged turn-1 outcome cannot become a verified turn-2 claim
turns: tool returns ok=True + 'probably succeeded' -> recorded failed

cases.scenario: Control: turn 1 completes honestly and the claim verifies. Turn 2 asserts the same claim again. Honest verification is idempotent — re-asserting a true claim still verifies.
cases.title: Honest claim re-asserted still verifies

cases.scenario: Turn 1: a tool fails honestly (ok=False) — recorded failed. Turn 2: retrying the SAME record is blocked (a retry needs a new action and a new approval). Turn 3: a NEW action with the same content under a NEW approval proceeds. The legitimate path stays open.
cases.title: Failed record blocked; new action with new approval proceeds

cases.scenario: Turn 1: an action completes honestly and its claim verifies. Turn 2: the recorded content is tampered with after completion. Turn 3: the claim is re-asserted and must be void — the content binding is re-checked at claim time.
cases.title: Post-completion tampering voids the claim across turns

cases.scenario: Turn 1: an operator correction (reconciliation) records that an unknown action did NOT complete. Turn 2: a completion claim is asserted for it anyway. The correction stands — the claim must not verify.
cases.title: Correction 'not done' voids any later completion claim

cases.scenario: Turn 1: an action is approved. Turn 2: Jack hits Stop. Turn 3: dispatch is attempted for the pre-Stop approval. Stop is deterministic — nothing approved before it survives it.
cases.title: Stop pressed after approval blocks the dispatch
Resume after Stop pauses across turns
cases.scenario: Turn 1: checkpoint. Turn 2: Stop. Turn 3: resume pauses (ASK) — no new plans off a pre-Stop snapshot.

cases.title: Fallback dispatch refused after its grant is revoked
